summary.title: Making a Chat App with Erlang, Rebar, Cowboy and Bullet
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a simple browser chat app in Erlang using Cowboy for HTTP, Bullet for WebSocket-style messaging, and a gen_event-based channel for pub/sub.
keywords: how to build chat app in erlang
takeaways: Add cowboy and bullet as rebar dependencies, list bullet in the application's applications list, and register a /chat bullet route with Cowboy.
Create a channel with gen_event so each bullet handler subscribes on init, unsubscribes on terminate, and receives broadcast messages.
Handle 'ping' messages by replying 'pong' only to the sender, while other messages are sent to all channel subscribers.
Serve a static chat page and jQuery/bullet.js client from priv/assets, connecting over ws://localhost:8080/chat, then build, run and test in multiple browsers.
summary.summary: The post is a continuation of an earlier Erlang/Rebar/Cowboy tutorial. It walks through adding the Cowboy and Bullet dependencies, registering a /chat route with a Bullet handler and serving static UI files under /ui. It then provides a simple HTML/jQuery page with a Bullet-based client script, a gen_event-based disrupt_channel module for pub/sub, and a disrupt_chat_handler that subscribes, relays messages and answers pings. The post ends with build and run commands and instructions to test the chat in two or more browsers.
